title: De-identify child blood-lead point data by coordinate rounding (Sacramento)
required_outputs: High_Blood_Level_Results_Rounded.shp (any point .shp/.gpkg/.geojson name accepted; the instruction names none)
method: Reproject the 373 points from Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) to WGS 84, add longitude/latitude fields, round them to two decimals (0.01 deg), rebuild point geometries at the rounded coordinates, save the de-identified layer, and document the reduction of unique locations: 372 -> 168 (204 fewer, 54.8 %).
benchmark_defects: The benchmark distributes only the .shp geometry files: no .dbf, so none of the 14 attribute columns listed in the dataset description (names, birthdays, blood level, ...) exist; no .shx/.prj either (the .shx and .prj files are reconstructed from the .shp files, CRS inferred from the coordinates).
The instruction names no output file; any point vector file in pred_results is accepted.
Sacramento_ZIP_Codes is only needed for context/visualisation.
checks: required: a point vector file written to pred_results
required: it holds the 373 records (or the 168 de-duplicated locations)
required: geometries in WGS 84 lie on the 0.01-degree grid (>= 99 %)
required: set of unique rounded locations equals the gold set (>= 98 % overlap both ways)
required: reduction documented (168 / 204-205 / 54.6-55.1 % / 45.0-45.2 % retained in a captured scalar incl. function locals, a <= 20-row table/dict/series, or a csv/txt/json/md output)
required: the published layer keeps no attribute reproducing the exact original coordinates (WGS 84 1e-5 deg / Web Mercator 1 m, off the 0.01-deg grid)
optional: rounded coordinate fields in the attribute table
